description: Chrysanthemum Tea, known as Jú Huā Chá in Chinese, is a fragrant herbal infusion cherished for its delicate floral aroma and cooling properties. This traditional beverage is widely enjoyed across China, especially during warmer months, offering a soothing and refreshing experience. It is believed to promote relaxation and aid in detoxification, making it a popular choice for health-conscious tea lovers.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chrysanthemum Flowers
instructions.text: Place the dried chrysanthemum flowers in a fine-mesh strainer. Gently rinse them under cool running water for a few seconds to remove any dust or impurities. This also helps to 'wake up' the flowers before steeping.

instructions.title: Boil Water
instructions.text: Bring 4 cups of filtered water to a rolling boil in a kettle or saucepan. The quality of water greatly impacts the taste of your tea, so filtered water is highly recommended for the best flavor.

instructions.title: Steep the Flowers
instructions.text: Transfer the rinsed chrysanthemum flowers into a heatproof teapot or a large mug. Carefully pour the hot boiling water over the flowers. Ensure all flowers are submerged.

instructions.title: Allow to Infuse
instructions.text: Cover the teapot or mug with a lid or saucer to trap the heat and aroma. Let the chrysanthemum flowers steep for about 5-7 minutes. For a stronger tea, you can steep for up to 10 minutes, but avoid over-steeping which can lead to bitterness.

instructions.title: Add Sweetener (Optional)
instructions.text: If you prefer your tea sweetened, add rock sugar or honey to taste while the tea is still hot. Stir gently until the sweetener is fully dissolved. You can start with a small amount and add more as desired.

instructions.title: Strain and Serve
instructions.text: Strain the tea into individual serving cups, removing the chrysanthemum flowers. You can leave a few flowers in each cup for presentation if desired. Serve immediately while hot, or let it cool to enjoy as a refreshing iced tea.

tips: For a stronger flavor, you can gently rinse the dried chrysanthemum flowers with a splash of hot water before the main steeping to remove any dust and open up the flowers.

Always use high-quality dried chrysanthemum flowers, preferably the 'Gong Ju' variety from Hangzhou, for the best aroma and flavor. Adjust the amount of rock sugar or honey to your personal preference; some prefer it unsweetened.
Chrysanthemum tea can be enjoyed hot or chilled. If serving cold, let it cool completely before refrigerating. It typically stays fresh in the refrigerator for up to 2-3 days.
